title: Main replacements to crews and years

blocks.text: A water utility (not GridCap) has approved a set of water-main replacements for the next three years and must now decide **which contractor crew does each job, and in which year**. Each job $`j`$ is done once, in one year, by one crew:

items: Job $`j`$ may be done in any year from `earliest` to `latest`, both included, and in no other year.
Crews work at different paces: crew $`c`$ needs $`d_{j,c}`$ weeks for job $`j`$ (`job.weeks[crew]`).
Crew $`c`$ has $`F_{c,t}`$ free weeks in year $`t`$ (`crew.weeks[year]`), and the jobs it does that year must fit in them.
A **large-diameter** main (`job.large`) may only be given to a **certified** crew (`crew.certified`).
Crew $`c`$ charges $`r_c`$ ($k per week), so job $`j`$ done by crew $`c`$ costs $`r_c\, d_{j,c}`$. The utility wants the cheapest schedule.

blocks.text: Write `build(jobs, crews, years)` in `schedule.py`. It returns the model and a dictionary `x` of binary variables keyed `(job id, crew id, year)`, where `x[j, c, t] = 1` means crew $`c`$ does job $`j`$ in year $`t`$. You decide which keys exist.

Each agent of this assignment is a crew *in a year*, with its own capacity. Write the formulation first: the sets (including the set of allowed job, crew and year triples), the parameters, the variable with its domain, the objective and each labelled row. Then code it.

The tests fix a schedule and ask the solver whether the model allows it; a schedule that needs a key your `x` does not have counts as refused. So any correct formulation passes, whether a forbidden triple has no variable or a row holding it at 0. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from schedule import Crew, Job, build

years = [2030, 2031]
crews = [Crew("Ortiz", {2030: 18, 2031: 12}, 8, certified=True), Crew("Patel", {2030: 14, 2031: 14}, 6)]
jobs = [Job("W1", 2030, 2031, {"Ortiz": 9, "Patel": 11}),
        Job("W2", 2030, 2030, {"Ortiz": 7, "Patel": 7}),
        Job("W3", 2031, 2031, {"Ortiz": 10, "Patel": 12}, large=True)]

model, x = build(jobs, crews, years)
print("variables:", sorted(x))
result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
print("status:", result.termination.reason.name)
print("cost:", round(result.objective_value(), 2))
values = result.variable_values()
print("schedule:", sorted(k for k, v in x.items() if values[v] > 0.5))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Job:
    jid: str
    earliest: int                  # first year the job may be done
    latest: int                    # last year the job may be done
    weeks: dict = field(default_factory=dict)    # crew -> weeks that crew needs for the job
    large: bool = False            # a large-diameter main: certified crews only


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Crew:
    cid: str
    weeks: dict                    # year -> weeks the crew is free that year
    rate: int                      # $k per week
    certified: bool = False


def build(jobs: list[Job], crews: list[Crew], years: list[int]) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    """Every job done once, by one crew in one year: in its window, by a crew allowed to, within the crew's weeks."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="crews-and-years")
    x: dict = {}
    # TODO: the variables, the rows and the cost.
    return model, x

if __name__ == "__main__":
    crews = [Crew("K1", {2027: 20, 2028: 20}, 9, certified=True)]
    model, x = build([Job("J1", 2027, 2028, {"K1": 8}, large=True)], crews, [2027, 2028])
    print(len(x), "variables")

cases.says: a schedule doing every job once is allowed, and one that leaves a job out is refused
a crew's jobs in one year, counted at that crew's own weeks per job, must fit its free weeks that year
a job scheduled in a year outside its window is refused
a large-diameter main given to an uncertified crew is refused, even with weeks to spare

origin.section: An Agent That May Not Take an Item Gets No Variable

concepts: pairs an agent may not take get no variable, and simple checks before solving catch tasks nobody can take
a generalized assignment gives every task to exactly one agent, with agent-dependent sizes and costs
